correction: The DONE status holds, but 'No functional defect seen' misses a regression the fix introduced. The new GraphQL list path (60633eff3) resolves the repository with `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner,url` before any list query runs. That command makes a network GraphQL call (measured 0.43-0.52 s here, confirmed with GH_DEBUG=api). Its cache is keyed by cwd and expires 10 minutes after the lookup, and access does not extend it. So the first page open after boot, and any open more than 10 minutes after the last resolution for that checkout, still runs two sequential gh waves (repo view, then 3 list queries) and 4 gh processes. The proposal targeted one round trip and 1-3 processes.
summary: The costs the finding describes are gone. The authored and review-requested lists no longer wait for git status: shouldReadInvolvementLists reads them while the provider is still unknown, and the route loader starts all three in parallel. Each list is a single GraphQL request with comments { totalCount } and stack info inline, so there are no comment bodies and no second stack call. A 30 s per-repository server cache dedupes concurrent identical reads. The worktree sweep that runs after a list read is now detached in the background process lane. One residual came with the fix: on a cold per-cwd repository cache, a `gh repo view` network round trip (~0.45-0.5 s) runs before the list queries. The cold first open is still two sequential gh waves, and this repeats every time the 10-minute TTL lapses.

evidence.note: shouldReadInvolvementLists returns true while provider === null, so the involvement reads start with the state list (proposal 1).
involvementEnabled uses the new gate. involvementSupported (:118) hides those rows until the host is known to support them. useGitStatus uses view 'summary', so there is no fetch.
The route loader runs prefetchPullRequestLists on enter. prefetchPullRequestLists.ts:84-98 watches all three list keys in parallel with the page chunk.
Rows select comments { totalCount } instead of bodies. Stack fields (:61) and checks are in the same document (proposal 2).
A plain or involvement list with no free-text query goes to github.listPullRequests (GraphQL with inline stack). enrichChangeRequestsWithStacks is not on this path.
The list RPC is wrapped in cachedRepositoryList, keyed by state, involvement, query, limit and picker. The repository key comes from the remote URL (GitManager.ts:1151-1216).
30 s TTL, concurrent reads join one in-flight call, failures are not cached, invalidated on remote refresh and mutations (proposal 3).
The linked-worktree sweep after a list read is forked detached in the background lane, so it is not on the response path (9a601cbd1).

RESIDUAL: listPullRequests first runs Cache.get(listRepositories, cwd). listRepositories (:1239) runs `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner,url`, a network GraphQL call measured at 0.43-0.52 s. It must finish before the list GraphQL can be built.
LIST_REPOSITORY_TTL = 10 min from lookup, keyed by cwd, with no stale-while-revalidate and no prewarm. Nothing else warms it: the PR index and branch lookups use the gh pr list paths.

fixDefects: Cold-path waterfall added by the fix. GitHubCli.listPullRequests (apps/server/src/sourceControl/GitHubCli.ts:1370), and also listIssues (:1434) and getPullRequestStates (:1342), awaits Cache.get(listRepositories, cwd) before the GraphQL list. On a miss that runs `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner,url` (:1239-1272), which makes a GraphQL network request: 0.43-0.52 s measured, confirmed with GH_DEBUG=api. The entry is keyed by cwd (each worktree pays separately) and expires 10 min after lookup (LIST_REPOSITORY_TTL, :76), with no background refresh. The 30 s list cache has also expired by then, so the first page open after boot, and any open more than 10 min after the last resolution for that checkout, is still two sequential gh waves with 4 gh processes. The finding's 'first open after boot ... in two waves' therefore still holds on the cold path, only with a cheaper first wave. Old gh pr list resolved the base repo inside its own process (no extra API call with a single remote). Minor residuals the auditor already noted: free-text and involvement+query search still use gh pr list with full comment bodies plus a sequential enrichChangeRequestsWithStacks call (GitHubSourceControlProvider.ts:588-621). That is not the page's first open. Proposal 4 (persistent or SWR seeding across restarts) is not implemented, and that part was optional.
implementationSketch:
Remove the repository-resolution round trip from the list critical path in apps/server/src/sourceControl/GitHubCli.ts.
(1) Resolve locally first. In the listRepositories lookup, before falling back to `gh repo view`, apply gh's own rules: if GH_REPO is set, use it. If a remote has `remote.<name>.gh-resolved` (`git config --get-regexp '^remote\..*\.gh-resolved$'`, where the value is 'base' or owner/repo), use that remote or value. If exactly one remote points at a GitHub host, use it. Parse with parseGitHubRepositoryIdentityFromUrl. Only an ambiguous setup (several GitHub remotes and no gh-resolved) calls `gh repo view`. The git reads are local and go through the git pool. Alternatively, pass the remote URL the registry already resolved (sourceControlProviders.resolveHandle -> handle.context.remoteUrl) into listPullRequests/listIssues as a hint.
(2) Make the cached identity stale-while-revalidate. After 10 min, keep serving it and refresh it with a background-lane fork, keeping the failure TTL. Optionally key it by the repository common dir so worktrees share one entry.
(3) If a list GraphQL call fails with 'Could not resolve to a Repository' (rename or transfer), invalidate the entry and retry once through `gh repo view`.
Tests in GitHubCli.test.ts: a single GitHub remote means listPullRequests makes no `repo view` call and issues the graphql call first. gh-resolved and GH_REPO are honoured. Ambiguous remotes fall back to one `repo view`. After the TTL (TestClock) a read is served from the stale identity while exactly one background `repo view` runs. A NOT_FOUND from the list triggers one re-resolution. Validate with focused vitest runs for GitHubCli and GitHubSourceControlProvider, and with GH_DEBUG=api timing of a cold PR page open (expect a single wave of 3 graphql requests).
decisionReason: Local server-side GitHub repository resolution and cache policy. No auth, E2EE, hosted lifecycle, Hub protocol or product trade-off. Matching gh's base-repo rules plus a gh repo view fallback keeps behaviour identical.
